summary: I measured the wheel's import graph and module structure with the medium's own facets: about 30 mentl runs, one at a time, with free memory checked before each. I then checked every facet verdict against whole-module reads, refs-of edges and the precomputed per-module doc answers. IMPORTS: the facet answers 258 rows (256 distinct edges). It marks 2 edges DEAD and both verdicts are false: canon.mn's only declaration is a let with 24 references. At least 10 of its 'used' verdicts are also false: main's five shipped-surface imports (which the unreachable facet itself reports as linked whole and never called), lower->search, io/json/lsp_frame->types and math->strings. infer.mn also carries 2 duplicate edges. The cause is that every module-structure facet, and audit, compares spans without module identity. LAYERS: six lib->src edges (three of them dead) put src/types.mn (5,384 lines) into every user program. Pulse's 16-module link carries it, and so does every lesson that imports io. The doc answers' own cost lines show the lessons judging at about 51 MB against the 207-line math module at 39 MB, and the page manifest ships src/types.mn as a lib. LINK MODELS: three different link models judge three different wheels: the src-first DAG, a lib-first blob of all of lib, and the battery's four-file text prefix. driver.mn says they read one input. The blob also judges three lib modules the compiler never links, one of them full of fabricated verdicts. EFFECTS: 86 effects, 20 with ops nothing performs (7 with none at all). Filesystem is bypassed at 7 call sites. Abort, catch_abort and lib/search form one dead subsystem across three modules. Effect names in rows are never resolved: persist's !Network and lesson 04's !Network both check clean. The compiler recognizes library effects by their spelling (10 'Alloc' literals in 7 modules). COHESION: four modules hold 53.3% of src, and lib/strings.mn hides five subsystems behind prefixes on 64 of its 100 declarations. PROSE: 139 comment references resolve nowhere across 19 modules, judged each as its own entry. 'walkthrough' appears in 32 comment cells (15 modules), '.mn:' in 34 (18 modules), 'commit' in 53. Some module headers contradict their own code, and 22 section banners serve as ledes, missed by a drift row that matches the wrong glyph. The course has two homes, and one lesson teaches three capabilities the medium deleted as false on 2026-10-02 (D4). SYNTAX's selective import and E_ImportNameCollision are not built. Overall: one root design dissolves most findings — modules as scopes, with non-transitive, name-carrying, layer-checked edges and one link model read from the DAG. The rest is putting each capability in one place and prose that names declarations rather than places.

findings.title: The facets that judge module structure compare spans with no module identity, so their import verdicts are wrong in both directions
sites: src/query.mn:1058-1061 (ref_is_outside; read by name_is_orphaned :1000-1001, op_is_performed :1051-1053 and decl_ref_verdict :719-720)
src/query.mn:615-633 (import_is_used and module_tail_eq: a module is identified by its last path segment)
src/pipeline.mn:828-830 (audit_walk: the extent is built from line numbers, the debt's module is discarded, tightenables are matched by name)
findings.class_size: 6 comparison sites with one shape: a position or a name compared without the module it belongs to. Measured on the wheel's link: both DEAD verdicts are false (infer->canon, parser->canon). At least 10 of the 256 'used' verdicts are false: main->dsp/feedback, dsp/signal, dsp/spectral, ml/tensor and math; lower->search; io->types; json->types; lsp_frame->types; math->strings
findings.current: refs_inside: `let sp = span_of_node_raw(hs[i]); if sp != span_zero() && span_overlaps(extent, sp) { true }`, so a reference at lines 1..8411 of ANY module counts as inside lower.mn. decl_names_of matches only FnStmt, TypeDefStmt, EffectDeclStmt and HandlerDeclStmt, then `_ => []`; canon.mn's only declaration is `let ty_string`, so canon 'brings nothing'. audit_walk: `filter({ (_modh, dspan, _, _) => span_overlaps(extent, dspan) }, debt)` throws away the module the debt carries. query.mn:585-590 concedes the facet cannot judge transitive conduits at all.
findings.ideal: A reference is an edge from a use cell to a declaration cell, and a declaration cell carries its home module: the handle collect_module_cells already stands on (D3/E4). `imports` then answers, per edge, the set of declarations that cross it: {d in refs_from(cells of A) | home(d) = B}, printed as `main -> io: print_string xN, …`. A dead edge is the empty set. unreferenced, performs and orphan-claims ask `home(site) != home(decl) || !inside(decl, site)` over (module, span) pairs, and audit keys debt and tightenables by declaration handle. No facet ever hands span_overlaps a bare span.
findings.law: PLAN §7 (the caret bullet, 2026-09-19): 'A position that is not module-qualified is not an address, and the medium held three machines that believed otherwise'. These six sites are further such machines. PLAN §2: re-resolving by name what an edge already connects is the canonical re-derivation
findings.evidence: The imports answer, read whole: 258 rows, including 'DEAD infer -> import canon' and 'DEAD parser -> import canon'. refs of ty_string -> 24 refs (parser:3351 and 23 in infer). refs of try_with_abort_catch -> 1 (search:134, which falls inside lower.mn's line range). refs of vec_sub -> ml/tensor:37, 52 and 57 only. The unreachable answer lists dsp/feedback 7, dsp/signal 18, dsp/spectral 6, math 20 and ml/tensor 19 as modules main links whole and never calls; the imports answer calls main's edges to all five 'used'. lib/io.mn, lib/json.mn, lib/lsp_frame.mn and lib/math.mn, read whole, reference no declaration of types or strings. strings' 100-declaration roster was read whole from its doc answer, and math's float_of_int has no declaring module.
findings.gate: Two facets of one medium may not disagree. A board bound refuses any edge the imports facet calls used into a module the unreachable facet calls linked-whole-never-called; it is born at the 5 measured and driven to 0. After the fix, the refs column returns each site with its module, so a module-blind comparison has nothing left to compare.

findings.title: The wheel's import graph carries dead, duplicate and manifest edges, and transitivity lets each pose as necessary
sites: src/main.mn:90, 92, 94, 96, 98 (dsp/feedback, dsp/signal, dsp/spectral, ml/tensor, math, under the 'shipped surface' comment at :84-87)
findings.class_size: Of the 258 rows, 2 are duplicates, and 10 of the 256 distinct edges are measured dead. Two more edges (src/main.mn:60 and src/pipeline.mn:61, both to dsp/clock) exist for handlers of an effect nothing performs (M9). The facet's own count is 2 dead, and both are false (M1).
findings.current: main.mn:84-87: 'The shipped surface — the stdlib the medium's binary carries whether or not the compiler's own body reaches it … The DAG that builds the medium IS the manifest of what the medium ships'. query.mn:586-588: 'imports are TRANSITIVE, so an edge carrying no referenced name of its own may still be the conduit by which a third module arrives'. Lesson 01-graph.mn:37 teaches '`int_to_str` and `print_string` come from io', but int_to_str is declared in lib/strings.mn and reaches the lesson only through io.mn:36's own import.
findings.ideal: An import is a non-transitive edge that names what crosses it, as in `import io {print_string}`. A module sees its own declarations, the names its edges select, and the prelude's one ambient edge. What a binary ships is a list of library roots, each judged as its own entry, never imports in the compiler's entry. A duplicate edge has no graph content of its own, so it format-lifts away. A dead edge is an over-declared dependency: the medium narrates it and `mentl tighten` deletes it, as it already writes a row clause's residue. A lesson that uses int_to_str writes `import strings {int_to_str}`, and the provenance it teaches is the edge.
findings.law: SYNTAX §Imports: selective import, and 'A name collision is resolved once, at the import edge'. SYNTAX §Diagnostic catalog: format-liftable ≡ MachineApplicable ∧ no graph node of its own. PLAN §2: 'A verb DRAWS an edge'
findings.evidence: src/infer.mn:26-54 read (15 import lines, two repeated). src/lower.mn:27-45 and src/main.mn:48-100 read. Each site's edge checked in the imports answer. lib/tutorial/01-graph.mn read whole (it imports io alone). lib/io.mn:34-36 imports types and strings. int_to_str appears in strings' doc roster.
findings.gate: T_DeadImport narrated at the edge (MachineApplicable; `mentl tighten` writes the deletion), plus a census CsDeadImport bounded at 0 in src/board.mn. A duplicate edge is canonicalized by fmt as a format-liftable class. Both read M1's per-edge name set, and with non-transitive edges no conduit exists to confuse them.

findings.title: The runtime library imports the compiler, and the resolver offers the compiler's modules to every user program
sites: src/driver.mn:39-82 (driver_module_path tries the direct file, src/, lib/, /mentl-home/src, /mentl-home/lib)
findings.class_size: 6 lib->src edges in src/main.mn's DAG (3 of them dead), plus 2 in lib/combinators.mn. Only two uses are live: clock's single report of a DiagKind constructor that exists for it alone, and lib/search's use of Abort, catch_abort and the graph trail (M8).
findings.current: Pulse's link is 16 modules, and one of them is `types` (src/types.mn: 5,384 lines of the compiler's metaschema). Every lesson that imports io links it through io.mn:34, which uses nothing from it. driver.mn:46-48 says 'a user project's `import prelude` reaches … its transitive `import types` (the substrate effect decls live in src/types.mn)'. In fact the prelude's closure is memory, strings, lists and threading; types arrives through io and dsp/clock. A user's `import graph` resolves to the compiler's src/graph.mn.
findings.ideal: Layer is a fact of the module node, read from its root: runtime (lib/), compiler (src/), or project. A runtime module imports only the runtime. A user program resolves against its own project and the runtime, never the compiler's root. Replay exhaustion is clock.mn's own failure: an abandoning op of the library's own effect, which the program's handler answers through AN-2's unwind. EReplayExhausted then leaves DiagKind. Once the three dead edges are also gone, Pulse's link loses types.mn entirely.
findings.law: PLAN §0: the developer is the telos, and a 44-line lesson judged with the compiler's metaschema in its link serves nobody. CLAUDE Anchor 4: build the wheel, never wrap the axle
findings.evidence:
The imports answer's edges dsp/clock->types, io->types, json->types, lsp_frame->types, search->types and search->own. lib/io.mn, lib/json.mn, lib/lsp_frame.mn and lib/dsp/clock.mn read whole. `mentl query examples/pulse/render/main.mn modules` -> 16 modules plus <link>, types among them. ide/space.manifest read: its 15 lib lines are exactly Pulse's link minus its main, src/types.mn included. The doc answers' own cost lines:
- lib/math (no types): 0.19 s, 39,464 KB
- lib/strings (no types): 0.25 s, 39,012 KB
- lib/json (dead edge to types): 0.36 s, 51,240 KB
- lesson 00-hello: 0.45 s, 51,092 KB
- lesson 01-graph: 0.36 s, 51,220 KB
- lesson 04-row: 0.47 s, 51,172 KB
Lessons of 40-73 lines judge about 12 MB heavier than the 207-line math module; their links differ by io (618 lines) and types (5,384). Timings were taken on a shared machine.
findings.gate: E_LayerInversion, armed at the import edge (a lib/ module naming a src/ module). It is born at zero once the three dead edges are deleted, clock's failure is re-homed, and lib/search and lib/combinators are deleted (M8, M10). The resolver stops trying src/ for an importer that is not a compiler module, so a user's `import graph` becomes E_MissingModule.

findings.title: Three link models judge three different wheels, and the comment that reconciles them is false
sites: src/main.mn:1397-1400 (propose and teach contracts take the module path)
findings.class_size: 3 link models across 6 sites, and 3 hardcoded `tutorial` exclusions. The blob judges at least 3 lib modules the compiler's DAG never links: lib/combinators.mn (329 lines), lib/audio/wav.mn (90) and lib/ml/grad.mn (34).
findings.current: march.sh concatenates `find lib -name '*.mn' -not -path '*/tutorial/*' | sort` and then `find src … | sort`: every lib module, lib first. driver.mn:297-306 says 'The pinned blob build concatenates `find src | sort` then `find lib | sort` … the sort fixes the WEAVE to the blob's own order, so the two build paths read one input', and :317 ranks src first with `str_contains(p, "src/")`. RESIDUE's Hβ.infer.order-independent-verdicts records that the blob was switched to lib-before-src on 2026-07-23, precisely because verdicts depend on order (that class closes only at rung 3). So `mentl compile src/main.mn` weaves the wheel in the order the fixed point abandoned. The battery's run contract compiles four files read by path and joined as text. That list is a hand copy of the prelude's closure that omits threading (imports edge 'prelude -> import threading'). The battery's propose and teach contracts go through the driver instead.
findings.ideal:
One link model. Every compile is the import DAG from an entry, plus the prelude edge, woven in the DAG's own topological order: dependencies first, and each cycle judged as one binding group, as rederive_cone already judges the session's cone. The fixed point is `mentl march` over src/main.mn's DAG. The battery judges each library module as its own entry, and a run fixture compiles from its module path like a propose fixture. Deleted:
- driver_canonical_order, with its key and insertion sort
- the blob assembly in march.sh and wt-env.sh
- battery_libs
- every `tutorial` test
lib-before-src then falls out of the layering (M3), never out of a path string.
findings.law: PLAN §11 Arc D (`Hβ.driver.link-is-reachability`): 'the demanded set read from import edges … A token allowlist is the Drift-8 disease wearing a linking costume'. PLAN §1/§6: the fixed point is the medium reproducing itself, so it must judge the medium that ships
findings.evidence: tools/march.sh:232-248 and tools/wt-env.sh:244-252 printed. src/driver.mn:290-321, src/main.mn:348-387, :1052-1065 and :1376-1415 read. RESIDUE.md:15517-15547 read. The imports answer has no row for combinators, audio/wav or ml/grad. PLAN §11's record of the refused single-pass cut names filter_list/filter_loop, map_list/map_loop and min_by_key among its 13 unresolved row gates. In the blob those names are lib/combinators.mn:205, :212, :227, :234 and :181, a module the compiler's DAG does not link. Dead library code shaped a landing's census.
findings.gate: Extend the march's verb-parity leg to compare the module set the fixed point judges with `mentl query src/main.mn modules`, and refuse any difference. With the battery's run contract going through the driver, a hand-listed prefix has nowhere to live.

findings.title: Seven call sites reach past the Filesystem capability, and its declaration, handler and implementation live in three different modules
sites: src/main.mn:362 and :378 (fs_list_dir_impl; the effect has no such op, src/types.mn:4588-4589)
findings.class_size: fs_read_file_impl has 8 refs: 1 handler arm and 7 bypasses in 4 modules. Two more calls go to fs_list_dir_impl, for an operation the effect never declared.
findings.current: types.mn:4591-4594: 'It was missing while three routes wrote files, which is the whole reason those routes reached past this effect to fs_create_impl'. The write side was closed; the read side was not. image_resume reads its wire with `let wire = fs_read_file_impl(path)`, and the battery reads every fixture the same way. Ops carry an `fs_` prefix and their bodies an `_impl` suffix because one namespace holds both.
findings.ideal: One module (lib/fs) holds `effect Filesystem { exists, read, write, mkdir, open, create, close, unlink, rename, list }` with its host handler beside it, and each arm's body IS the implementation, so there is no separately callable `_impl` to reach past. A file read is then either a Filesystem perform or raw WASI, which `!WASI` already catches. A sandbox, a test double or the session's in-memory tree installs its own handler, and every read obeys it. With modules as scopes the ops are simply `read` and `write`, qualified by the import edge rather than a prefix.
findings.law: types.mn:4352: 'the effect-beside-handler law'. PLAN §4④ and §2: persistence is a handler swap, and the handler IS the backend; a read that skips the effect cannot be redirected by the handler its route installs
findings.evidence: `mentl query src/main.mn "refs of fs_read_file_impl"` -> pipeline:848, persist:93, main:1062 (x4), main:1390, dsp/cfc:277. Read: src/pipeline.mn:840-865, src/types.mn:4570-4599, src/main.mn:348-387, :1061-1062 and :1388-1390, and lib/persist.mn:76-97.
findings.gate: Once the implementation lives in the arms, there is no name to bypass. Until then, a census of `_impl` references outside their declaring module, bounded in src/board.mn at the 9 measured and ratcheting to 0.

findings.title: Effect names in rows are never resolved: a negation can name an effect nothing in the link declares, and the medium checks it clean
findings.class_size: 2 authored rows measured naming an undeclared effect. `IO` is given meaning at 3 compiler sites and declared by no module. A full count needs a facet (verb gap).
findings.current: `mentl where lib/persist.mn Network` -> 'error: not found: Network — no declaration of it', with exit 0. `mentl check lib/persist.mn` and `mentl check lib/tutorial/04-row.mn` exit 0 and say nothing. Network is declared only in lib/dsp/signal.mn, outside both links. persist's `!Filesystem` resolves only through the dead io->types conduit (`mentl where lib/persist.mn Filesystem` -> types:4576).
findings.ideal: An effect name in a row is a reference. Its position is a cell that inference binds to the effect's declaration in the module's scope (PLAN §11's 'positions are cells'), and an unresolved name is E_MissingVariable at the name. Negation then works by declaration identity: `!Network` forbids the Network this module can see, and two modules' same-named effects are two different effects.
findings.law: SYNTAX §«Named effect rows»: 'a row referencing an undeclared effect surfaces `E_MissingVariable` at the unresolved name'. CLAUDE drift 3 (an effect-name set held as flat strings). PLAN §0 property 2
findings.evidence: The five commands quoted above. lib/persist.mn:76-97 and lib/tutorial/04-row.mn read whole. src/intern.mn:59-79, src/mentl.mn:943-978 and src/types.mn:4328-4350 read.
findings.gate: E_MissingVariable armed at an unresolved row name. It is born at zero on the wheel once persist's gate names only effects its link declares. The ghosts count ratchets down as row positions become cells.

findings.title: The compiler recognizes library effects by their spelling, so a user's same-named effect inherits a projection, and the medium's vocabulary has no module
sites: src/effects.mn:1544-1558 (projection_of_effects: Thread, Simd, Gpu, Persist, Derivative, Alloc)
src/intern.mn:70 (medium_vocabulary: Memory, Alloc, IO, Network, Trap, Arena)
`"Alloc"` literals at backends/wasm:1142, 1221, 1230; effects:1554; infer:5272, 11911; intern:70; lower:1726; mentl:964; types:4288
findings.class_size: 10 `"Alloc"` literals in 7 modules; 6 projection spellings; 4 severance spellings, 2 of which (IO, Network) no compiler-linked module declares. Intrinsics also have no declaring module (float_of_int).
findings.current: effects.mn:1537-1539: 'The class is recognized by the effect a handler answers, so a program that declares its own Thread or Derivative effect gets the same reading'. `mentl where lib/math.mn float_of_int` prints `float_of_int(_)` with its widths and no address. Lesson 04-row.mn:9 teaches 'The compiler does not know what `Alloc` means', which the ten literals contradict.
findings.ideal: The medium's vocabulary is a set of declarations in ONE ambient substrate module, resolved to handles once, when the prelude edge is drawn. Every compiler reader holds the handle, never the spelling. A projection class is a fact of the effect's declaration: lib/threading's Thread IS the schedule effect by identity, so a user's own `effect Thread` is an ordinary dispatched effect. The severance labels are written beside the effects they describe. An intrinsic is a declaration with an intrinsic body in that module, so every name a program can say has a home that `where` can address.
findings.law: CLAUDE drift 3 and drift 8 (string-keyed). PLAN §11 6.1 made an EffName a handle, but it is a handle of the spelling, so identity still rides the string
findings.evidence: `mentl query src/main.mn "text Alloc"` (10 literals). src/effects.mn:1525-1560, src/intern.mn:50-85 and src/mentl.mn:940-980 read. `mentl where lib/math.mn float_of_int`.
findings.gate: A census of string literals in src that spell an effect, bounded at 0 once the vocabulary is held as handles. A frontier fixture that declares its own `effect Thread` and installs a handler for it, contracted to run as an ordinary dispatch.

findings.title: Effects nothing performs stay declared and installed, and one of them makes the compiler import a DSP library
sites: src/main.mn:212-219 (interrogate_default installed; its comment says cursor_default performs Interrogate ops)

Six of those seven are library effects that reach the compiler only through dead, surface or marker edges. 13 are partial: Format 1/3, Workspace 3/11, Interact 4/10, SharedMemory 1/7, CursorRead 2/3, Memory 19/24, GraphWrite 35/39, Thread 2/3, Tick 1/2, Deadline 1/2, InferCtx 22/23, EnvRead 5/6, LowerScope 23/24.

findings.ideal: An install that absorbs nothing its extent performs is visible to the row, because the subtraction is empty. The medium narrates it where it stands, and `mentl tighten` deletes it. A marker for the clock calculus is written when the calculus actually reads it.

findings.evidence: `refs of no_iter_context` -> 7 sites, all in main.mn. The performs answer read whole. lib/dsp/clock.mn read whole. src/main.mn:180-221 and src/pipeline.mn:1-70 read.

Comments cite 4 deleted homes (src/oracle.mn, lib/net.mn, std/compiler/types.mn, docs/specs) and the deleted seed.
findings.current:
Contradictions read this session:
- pipeline.mn:18-19 claims to own lookup_ty_graph, but `mentl where src/main.mn lookup_ty_graph` answers 'handler lookup_ty_graph absorbs LookupTy, answers a at graph:2516'.
- types.mn:4334 cites src/oracle.mn's project_queue_merger, and `mentl where src/main.mn project_queue_merger` finds nothing.
- io.mn:24 says 'Effects declared in std/compiler/types.mn — not re-declared here', directly above `effect WASI` at :45.
- io.mn:9-11 calls the image never-freeing and cites net.mn as precedent; the arena landed 2026-10-03 and net.mn was deleted 2026-10-05.
- main.mn:189-190 says patch_echo is used 'today' and names patch-to-file a follow-up, while :211 installs patch_to_file.
- math.mn:6-9 says every float operation routes through float_add/float_mul, but math.mn's own bodies use the native operators, and no such function is in strings' roster.

findings.ideal: Prose names declarations, never places. A path or a line number copies an address the graph already holds and rots at the next edit; a commit hash belongs to the ledger; a spec number or a walkthrough is archaeology. A claim about a module's contents — which handlers it owns, which modules it reaches — is a projection (`mentl where`, `mentl query <entry> modules`), so the header stops making it. What stays in the comment is the author's intent.
findings.law: SYNTAX §Comments: a comment 'shows what IS, not what was', and lifecycle vocabulary is forbidden. CLAUDE: 'comments must be TRUE'. CLAUDE ⟳: 'A MECHANISM-COMMENT is the same confession at the prose layer'
findings.evidence: The three prose answers read whole. The two where answers. git log: src/oracle.mn deleted at 43e371c9, lib/net.mn at 30b43db4. std/compiler/types.mn, docs/specs, docs/errors, INSIGHTS.md, bootstrap and tools/runner are absent. The file at each site was read.
findings.gate: Extend doc-truth to .mn comments as census shapes: a path token naming no file, a `name.mn:N` citation, a hex commit token, and a `spec NN` citation, each bounded and ratcheted to 0. Add a `mentl tighten` arm that rewrites a file:line citation into the name of the declaration at that address, which the address surface already resolves.

findings.title: SYNTAX's module system is not built: no selective import and no edge-local collision, so the whole link is one namespace, refused four ways and paid for in prefixes
sites: src/driver.mn:1-22 ('concatenates the DAG into ONE program'; the per-module env overlay still open)
lib/json.mn (json_escape_len, json_escape_emit, json_escape_tail, beside strings' escape_len, escape_emit, escape_tail)
findings.class_size: Selective import and E_ImportNameCollision are both absent; neither appears among the 75 DiagKind constructors. 4 link-wide collision refusals stand where one edge-local refusal belongs. Prefixes: 64 declarations in lib/strings.mn, 13 json_ in lib/json.mn, 9 fs_ ops.
findings.current: parse_import_path joins identifier segments on TSlash and stops, so `{a, b}` does not parse. EOpShadowsOp's own message: 'The env holds one entry per name, so the second declaration REPLACES the first rather than joining it: every existing call to `{name}` is now judged against `{now}`'s signature, and the errors surface wherever those calls are — inside the library, at spans your program never wrote. Rename this op'. EDuplicateFnName: 'a second `fn {name}` in one namespace … rename one'. query.mn:580-583: 'A user's `effect Backtrack { abort() }` lost silently to the compiler's Abort'.
findings.ideal:
Modules are scopes. `import io {print_string, read_stdin}` draws one edge per name, and a bare import brings in the module's declarations. Two edges binding one name in one module is E_ImportNameCollision at the second edge: the only collision refusal, local to the importer, with narrowing the import as its Quick Fix. Each module's names are its own:
- json's escape_len and strings' escape_len coexist
- a user's Abort never meets the compiler's
- ops lose their fs_ prefix, and `_impl` disappears with M5
The open per-module env overlay is exactly this, and the session's per-module registration (E2) is its first half.
findings.law: SYNTAX §Imports: selective import, and 'A name collision is resolved once, at the import edge, not re-derived at N call sites'. SYNTAX's hard-error table lists E_ImportNameCollision

root_designs:
MODULES ARE SCOPES, AND AN IMPORT IS A NON-TRANSITIVE EDGE THAT NAMES WHAT CROSSES IT. Every declaration cell carries its home module. Every use cell — an expression name, an effect name in a row, a type in an annotation, a backticked name in a comment — is an edge to a declaration handle, resolved in the using module's scope: its own declarations, the names its import edges select (`import io {print_string}`), and the prelude's one ambient edge. Answers to the brief's three questions:
- Imports are not transitive, so a conduit cannot exist and a lesson's provenance is its own edge.
- A duplicate import has no graph content and format-lifts away. A dead import is an over-declared dependency: narrated (T_DeadImport) and deleted by `mentl tighten`, the same class as an over-declared row. Refusing it would make an unfinished edit unsayable mid-session.
- Op names drop the fs_ prefix, and str_/float_/set_/json_ become module names. WASI op names (fd_write) stay, because they are the host ABI's own names, not prefixes.
Collisions are refused once, at the importing edge (E_ImportNameCollision). This design dissolves:
- M1 (`imports` becomes the per-edge name set)
- M2 (dead, duplicate and conduit edges)
- M6 (unresolved row names)
- M7 (spelling-keyed vocabulary)
- M12 (the 139 unresolved comment references)
- M16 (the four link-wide collision refusals and the prefix tax)
It builds on what exists: positions becoming cells (PLAN §11's order, 18,681 ghosts), the parent edge, the module handle collect_module_cells already carries, the per-module E_MissingImport, and the session's per-module registration. RESIDUE already names the design: Hβ.driver.per-module-env-overlay.

LAYER IS A FACT OF THE MODULE NODE, AND THE IMPORT EDGE READS IT. The runtime (lib/) sits below the compiler (src/). A runtime module imports only the runtime. A user project resolves against its own root and the runtime, never the compiler's root, so the /mentl-home/src fallback in driver_module_path disappears. E_LayerInversion is armed at the edge. This removes src/types.mn from every user link (M3; about 12 MB per lesson judgment), the compiler's graph trail from a library (M8), and the manifest's `lib src/types.mn`. It also gives M4's topological weave lib-before-src by construction, instead of by `str_contains(p, "src/")`.

ONE LINK MODEL, READ FROM THE DAG. Every compile — the fixed point, `mentl compile`, a battery fixture, a lesson on the page — is the import DAG from an entry plus the prelude edge, woven in the DAG's topological order with each cycle judged as one binding group, as the session's cone already is. The fixed point is `mentl march` over src/main.mn's DAG; the battery judges each library module as its own entry; what the medium ships is a list of library roots. This deletes the blob assembly in march.sh and wt-env.sh, driver_canonical_order with its order key, battery_libs' text prefix, the three tutorial tests and main.mn's surface imports. It takes combinators, wav and grad out of the fixed point (M4, M10, M15).

A CAPABILITY IS ONE MODULE: THE EFFECT, ITS HANDLER, AND ITS IMPLEMENTATION AS THE HANDLER'S ARMS. No `_impl` function exists to reach past the effect. An effect nothing performs is deleted with its installs; an install that absorbs nothing is narrated; the performs facet becomes a board bound. This dissolves:
- M5: the Filesystem bypass and its three homes
- M8: the Abort/catch_abort/search subsystem
- M9: IterContext's seven installs, the compiler's import of dsp/clock, and the Interrogate effect
It also gives the Severance Map modules that are capability units (M11).

PROSE NAMES DECLARATIONS, NEVER PLACES, AND A MODULE'S PROSE BELONGS TO THE MODULE NODE. Paths, line numbers, commit hashes, spec numbers and walkthrough references become census shapes that doc-truth counts inside .mn comments, each bound ratcheting to 0. `mentl tighten` rewrites a file:line citation into the declaration at that address. Prose above a module's first declaration, or set off by a blank line, is the module's lede. fmt strips decorative rules, and a section becomes a module. This dissolves M13 and M14, closes M12's nonexistent-name class, and keeps the lessons honest once they carry contracts (M15).
verb_gaps: `imports` per edge: the declarations crossing an edge, module-qualified (e.g. `mentl query <entry> "edge main -> io"`). Today the facet returns one boolean per edge, and it is module-blind (M1)

`importers of <module>`: reverse import edges across the whole repository. No facet can say who imports lib/combinators.mn, lib/audio/wav.mn or lib/ml/grad.mn, because every facet answers inside one entry's link
`unresolved-effects`: effect names in rows that resolve to no declaration in the link. persist's `!Network` passes check, and only a per-name `where` finds it

prose by class rather than by substring: a path naming no file, a `name.mn:N` citation, a hex commit token, a `spec NN` citation. `prose seed` answered 161 cells spanning six different meanings of the word
`clusters`: intra-module reference clustering, so module cohesion is measured rather than asserted (M11)
`ledes`: each declaration's lede across a link, with a banner test. The 22 banner ledes here were counted by reading three doc answers by hand
unreferenced and performs over types and effects: annotation and row positions are ghosts, so every type and effect reads as unreferenced
`mentl where` exits 0 when it answers 'not found'. The exit code should carry the verdict, as `mentl accept` already does
a duplicate-import census: infer.mn's two duplicate edges were found by reading
the fixed point's module set compared with `mentl query src/main.mn modules`: what the blob judges that the compiler's DAG does not
names with no declaring module: `mentl where lib/math.mn float_of_int` prints a head and no address, and nothing lists the intrinsics that have no home
facet self-consistency: `imports` calls five of main's edges used, while `unreachable` calls the same modules linked whole and never called. The medium could check its facets against each other
`mentl doc <module>` renders declarations only, so a module header has nowhere to appear and lands as the first declaration's lede
